'''Feng Duan''' ({{zh|s=冯端}}; 11 June 1923 – 15 December 2020) was a physicist of China, an expert in solid-state physics.<ref>[http://www.chinavitae.com/biography/Feng_Duan|894 Feng Duan] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210228162436/https://chinavitae.com/biography/Feng_Duan%7C894 |date=2021-02-28 }}, chinavitae.com, accessed December 2010</ref> He was a member of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]. He was a delegate to the [[6th National People's Congress|6th]], [[7th National People's Congress|7th]] and [[8th National People's Congress]].<ref>{{cite news|author1=Ma Haoge ({{lang|zh|马浩歌}})|url=https://www.bjnews.com.cn/detail/160810570415610.html |script-title=zh:著名物理学家、中科院院士冯端逝世 享年98岁 |work=bjnews.com.cn |date=16 December 2020 |access-date=16 December 2020 |language=zh}}</ref>

==Etymology==
Because he was born before the [[Dragon Boat Festival]] ({{zh|s=端午节|p=Duān Wǔ Jié|labels=no}}), so his father named him "Duan".<ref name="carrot"/>

==Biography==
Feng was born in [[Suzhou]], [[Jiangsu]], though his ancestral hometown is [[Shaoxing]], [[Zhejiang]].<ref name="carrot">{{cite news|author1=Bei Jiang ({{lang|zh|北绛}})|url=http://news.sciencenet.cn/htmlnews/2014/12/308654.shtm |script-title=zh:冯焕冯慧冯康冯端：冯门四杰传佳话 |work=sciencenet.cn |date=5 December 2014 |access-date=16 December 2020 |language=zh}}</ref> His father Feng Zupei ({{zh|s=冯祖培|labels=no}}) was an official in the [[Nationalist government]].<ref name="carrot"/> Feng has two elder brothers. All of them were alumni of National Central University.<ref name="carrot"/> The eldest, [[Feng Huan]] went to United States in 1947, and served in GE R&D center as a senior engineer.<ref name="carrot"/> His second elder brother, [[Feng Kang]], was a prominent Chinese mathematician, and also a member of CAS.<ref name="carrot"/> His elder sister Feng Hui ({{zh|s=冯慧|labels=no}}) was a researcher at the Institute of Zoology, Chinese Academy of Sciences.<ref name="carrot"/> His brother-in-law [[Ye Duzheng]] was a meteorologist and a member of CAS.<ref name="carrot"/> In 1942, after graduating from Suzhou High School, Feng entered [[National Central University]] (renamed [[Nanjing University]] after 1949), studying physics. He graduated in 1946 and stayed at the University, serving as a teaching assistant in physics department. Later, he became a lecturer, an associate professor, and eventually attained the title of professor. Feng was the president of graduate school of Nanjing University, and the director of state key laboratory of solid-state micro-structure physics. He used to serve as president of China Physics Society, first scientist of "Nano Material Science", a "climbing project" of National Commission of Science and Technology, and the chairman of [[Jiangsu]] Science and Technology Association. Feng was elected to member of Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) in 1980. 

Feng was the chairman of alumni association of National Central University. 

Feng died on December 15, 2020, in [[Nanjing]], [[Jiangsu]], aged 97.

==Personal life==
Feng married Chen Lianfang ({{zh|s=陈廉方|labels=no}}) in Nanjing on April 1, 1955.<ref name="wife">{{cite news|author1=Zong Qing ({{lang|zh|宗青}})|url=https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_4614833 |script-title=zh:97岁院士冯端为妻子写诗65年，文学和艺术造诣同样精深 |work=thepaper.cn |date=7 October 2019 |access-date=5 December 2020 |language=zh}}</ref> Chen was a high school Chinese teacher and graduated from department of foreign language of National Central University in 1945.<ref name="wife"/>

==Honours and awards==
* 1980 Member of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] (CAS)
* 1993 member of [[The World Academy of Sciences]] (TWAS)
